clue.text: Current attraction exhibit at the sciencefair

definitions.text: Current attraction exhibit at the sciencefair

parts.words: Current attraction exhibit at the sciencefair
parts.note: an electric current through a coil makes a magnet that attracts iron, a favourite demonstration at school science fairs

explanation.surface: The most popular stand at the science fair right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current attraction' reads as 'today's big draw', but means pulling power produced by an electric current. 'sciencefair' is the newspaper's run-together 'science fair'.
explanation.definitionFit: This device is a coil that becomes magnetic, attracting iron, only while electric current flows through it.

clue.text: Fieldsman who hasn't bowled recently

definitions.meaning: a cricket fielder placed deep on the off side, behind the bowler
a bowler kept out of the attack for some time

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket it is a deep fielding position on the off side, and a bowler rested from the attack has been off for ages.

clue.text: Meat axe

definitions.meaning: a cutlet of pork or lamb on the bone
to cut or cancel, as a job or project

explanation.definitionFit: A cutlet of meat on the bone shares its name with a cutting blow, and to axe a scheme is to cut it.

clue.text: The yuppy revolution means an artist has to copy originals

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
to trace is to copy an original by drawing over it

explanation.surface: An artist copies old masters in the name of a 1980s social upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests upheaval, but means going round and round, as in an endless competitive scramble for success.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the endless competitive scramble for career success, the life associated with young upwardly mobile professionals.

clue.text: 1000 ducks encircle the harbour

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the round 0, so two ducks are two Os
to ring is to encircle

explanation.surface: A thousand ducks surround the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a nought in cricket, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooring is a place where a boat is tied up, much as a harbour shelters it.

clue.text: The way she walks gives Georgia sex appeal

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
it is old slang for sex appeal, from the film star Clara Bow, the It girl

explanation.surface: A Southern belle's walk shows off her allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal comes from the 1927 film 'It'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's manner of walking, their stride or step, is their gait.

clue.text: Mince pie and salt for one who enjoys food

indicators.note: to mince is to chop finely, so the letters are chopped up and rearranged

parts.note: to salt meat or fish is to cure it

explanation.surface: Mince pie and salt, a meal for someone who loves eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince pie' reads as the Christmas pastry, but 'Mince' is the instruction to rearrange PIE into EPI.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a gourmet, a person of refined taste in eating and drinking.

clue.text: Brief success, then the fat is in the fire

definitions.meaning: a short-lived triumph that comes to nothing

definitions.text: the fat is in the fire
definitions.meaning: read literally, a sudden flare of burning fat in a frying vessel

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a short-lived success and, taken literally, a burst of flame when cooking fat catches fire.

clue.text: Deem notes best settlement

indicators.note: settlement means the letters settle into a new order

explanation.surface: Judging banknotes the best way to settle up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' rearranges DEEM NOTES BEST and also describes paying off what is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying off what one owes is settling one's accounts, as debts are settled with notes.

clue.text: What the switchboard girl is asked for at Rugby

definitions.text: What the switchboard girl is asked for at Rugby

parts.words: What the switchboard girl is asked for at Rugby
parts.note: a caller asks the telephone operator for an outside connection, and in rugby the same phrase names the throw-in where forwards stand in two rows

explanation.surface: A caller at Rugby School asks the telephone operator to put a call through.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is a town and school in England that gave its name to the game; the set piece there is the throw-in from touch, while the switchboard request is for an outside connection.
explanation.definitionFit: Telephone exchanges gave callers an external connection, and in rugby union the restart from touch has the forwards form two parallel rows.

clue.text: Opening condition with no rice about

parts.note: no is zero, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: the word rice is placed about the other piece, wrapping around it

parts.note: if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: An opening whose state means there is no rice around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you to wrap the grain around the conditional word; 'no' is read as zero and so gives the round letter that starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole or aperture in the body or in a vessel is an opening.

clue.text: American news should be back any time now

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'American news should be back any time now' (4): no reading of 'American news' reversed gives NOOS, so a word looks misread; the scan is not available.
annotationWithheld.clue: American news should be back any time now

clue.text: Frenzied offer made for Burlington House

parts.note: Burlington House in London is the home of the Royal Academy, abbreviated RA
a bid is an offer, as at an auction

explanation.surface: Someone makes a wild offer to buy a famous London building.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House, on Piccadilly in London, houses the Royal Academy of Arts, so it stands for RA; the bid comes first in the clue but last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid describes a mad, furious, fanatical state, like that of a dog with rabies.

clue.text: Leave free

definitions.meaning: to depart from or abandon a place or job
an old adjective sense: rid of, released from an obligation

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to depart or resign and, as an adjective, to be rid of something, as in 'well rid of'.

clue.text: Head-dressed poultry

definitions.meaning: read as two words, wearing a hat on one's head
a castrated cockerel fattened for the table

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the word says someone has a hat in place; whole, it is a castrated cockerel raised for eating.

clue.text: Give pound in fare in a flash!

indicators.note: in says the letter for a pound sits inside the cost of travel

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Pay a pound towards a fare in a hurry!
explanation.walkthrough: L for pound comes from the Latin libra, as in the £ sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A flare is a sudden blaze of light, a brief flash.

clue.text: Blow up fashionable apartment at Exmouth

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a flat is a British word for an apartment

indicators.note: at the start of Exmouth is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone talks up a trendy seaside flat in a Devon town.
explanation.walkthrough: Exmouth is a seaside town in Devon; 'at Exmouth' gives only the E it starts with, a loose old-style signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a balloon or tyre is to fill it with air.

clue.text: Earth in a gallon vessel

indicators.note: the letter for earth goes in the middle of the measure of volume

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: Soil held in a container of one gallon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' seems to be the gallon container, but it means a ship: the old Spanish sailing kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sailing ship of the 16th century, especially a Spanish treasure ship, is a kind of seagoing vessel.

clue.text: US stock assigned to a dense clump

indicators.note: the letters are assigned new places, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: American shares allocated to a tight bunch of investors.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussock is a thick tuft of grass growing in a dense clump.

clue.text: Boards the child of a former marriage

definitions.meaning: read as two words, treads upon

definitions.text: the child of a former marriage
definitions.meaning: a partner's son from an earlier marriage

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the word means treads upon or boards; whole, it is a spouse's son from an earlier marriage.

clue.text: Slaughter which makes a monarch get sick inside

indicators.note: inside places the word for unwell within the word for a ruler

parts.note: a king is a monarch
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A massacre that makes a ruler feel nauseous.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing is the act of slaying, a slaughter.

clue.text: Only a priest could be disposed to forgive their main crimes

definitions.text: Only a priest could be disposed to forgive their main crimes

indicators.note: disposed here means arranged, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Only a clergyman would be inclined to pardon the offences of these people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' looks like 'inclined', but arranges A PRIEST; 'main' is the sea, so their crimes are at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea robbers commit their crimes on the main, the old word for the open ocean.

clue.text: Place under attack

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A town besieged.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder is to raid and pillage, an attack in order to rob.

clue.text: Big game takes in everyone of the highest standing

indicators.note: takes in means the match word contains the word for everybody

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket or rugby match
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A major match admits all those of the top rank.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a top international fixture in cricket or rugby; 'standing' hints at rank, but here means height.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing highest means being the greatest in height.

clue.text: Dusk is calm and unruffled

definitions.meaning: ..., in its old poetic shortened form

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a poetic form of evening, the time of dusk, and also means level, steady and calm in temper.

clue.text: of nimbus, cumulus, etc

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'of nimbus, cumulus, etc' (5) is cut short: the opening words, which hold the definition or the rest of the wordplay, are missing, and no scan is available.

clue.text: A Confederate general veering towards the sheltered side

parts.note: Robert E. Lee commanded the Confederate armies in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A Southern general changing course in the Civil War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'veering' is only a link that fits the sailing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, the lee side is the one sheltered from the wind, so moving that way is to leeward.

clue.text: Illness accounting for two-thirds of the plague

indicators.note: two-thirds of the six-letter word keeps four letters, dropping its first two

explanation.surface: A sickness making up most of the plague.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old word for malarial fever with shivering fits, an illness.

clue.text: Whereon one expects to be given woven leis?

definitions.text: Whereon one expects to be given woven leis?

indicators.note: woven means the letters are twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: A place where one expects to receive garlands of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges LEIS; garlands of flowers are given to visitors to Hawaiian islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Visitors to Pacific islands such as Hawaii are given flower garlands on arrival.

clue.text: Pack animal for example with first rate native weapon

parts.note: an ass, or donkey, carries packs
eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
A1 is first rate, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A donkey, say, carrying a top-quality local spear.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class; crosswords often read the digit 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is the slender iron-tipped spear of southern African peoples.

clue.text: Locked up for the final course

indicators.note: up says the word for having locks is turned around, read from its end

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair, so locked means tressed

explanation.surface: Imprisoned for the last part of a programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locked up' reads as jailed, but 'Locked' means having locks of hair (tressed), and 'up' turns it round to give DESSERT.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet dish served at the end of a meal is its last course.

clue.text: Concealed habits assumed to protect the skin

definitions.text: Concealed habits assumed to protect the skin

parts.words: Concealed habits assumed to protect the skin
parts.note: habits are clothes, worn hidden beneath others and put on next to the body

explanation.surface: Secret habits someone adopts to protect themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' suggests behaviour but means clothing, as a monk's habit; 'assumed' means put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Vests, slips and pants are clothing worn hidden beneath outer clothes, next to the body.
